title: Generation of precision-cut slice cultures of human placenta
protocol: Immediately after birth, cut biopsies of around 5 cm diameter from the human placenta halfway between the umbilical cord insertion and the margin of the placenta using sterile scissors.
Ensure each placental biopsy includes the full thickness of the placenta with both maternal and fetal sides.
Store placenta biopsies in sterile PBS containing antibiotics at 4°C until processing to preserve tissue viability.
Process placental tissue inside a biological safety cabinet.
Rinse the placenta biopsies with cold sterile PBS supplemented with antibiotics until the surrounding blood is cleared off.
Manipulate the placental tissue only at the borders of the fetal membranes using sterile blunt-end forceps to avoid harming the tissue.
Cut placental tissue into smaller pieces using a sterile blade, preserving the orientation of the maternal-fetal interface.
Store the placenta pieces on ice until further processing.
Ensure each piece weighs approximately 1–1.8 g and measures 0.8–1 cm x 0.8–1 cm, with a thickness of 2 cm representing full placental thickness.
Prepare multiple tissue pieces as needed to obtain the required number of slices per embedded piece of placenta.
Do not store small placenta specimens in PBS or culture media before embedding, as this can impair the cutting process.
Embed placental tissue into an agarose solution kept at 37°C inside a biological safety cabinet.
Pour 1.5 mL of 1% agarose solution into a Peel-A-Way embedding mold to cover the bottom.
Place the mold on ice.
Wait approximately 60 ± 5 seconds for the agarose solution to start solidifying.
Place the placenta piece horizontally in the middle of the mold containing the initial layer of agarose solution.
Cover the tissue with approximately 3 mL of 1% agarose solution.
Keep the mold on ice until the agarose solution fully solidifies.
Fill the buffer tray of the tissue slicer with cold sterile culture media and place it into the ice tray.
Cover the filled buffer tray with a Plexiglas lid to avoid any ice in the culture media.
Fill the ice tray with crushed ice.
Cut at the edges of the mold and down the corners.
Open the mold and carefully detach the agarose block.
Glue the agarose block on the specimen plate.
Transfer the agarose block on the specimen plate into the buffer tray containing media or PBS supplemented with antibiotics.
Optionally, trim the agarose using a blade or scalpel before gluing it onto the specimen plate.
Discard the first 1–2 sections during sectioning as they do not have the defined thickness.
Support slices gently with a sterile brush during sectioning to avoid pushing down the tissue and disrupting contact with the blade.
Cut any slice that did not fully detach from the specimen block using a sterile surgical scissor.
Collect floating slices using a flat sterile brush and transfer them into a 6-well plate as cutting progresses.
Use the top of a sterile 1 mL pipette tip to punch precision-cut slices.
Position the pipette tip in the middle of the slice.
Push down the pipette tip while gently turning it to obtain a precision-cut slice.
Discard the surrounding tissue after punching.
Place each punched slice in 4 mL of culture media in a single well of a 6-well plate.
Culture the slices at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Maintain the cultures at 37°C, 5% CO2 for two days prior to use.
Change the media every 24 hours.
